sections.evidence:
- D06 (Comment 1, baseline quotas) [c1]: "NMFS received multiple comments supporting the increased U.S. bluefin tuna baseline quota from 1,316.14 mt to 1,509.98 mt"
- D06 (Table 5, baseline row) [c1]: "Baseline Quota.......................... 1,316.14 1,509.98"
- D06 (note to Table 5, bycatch allocations) [c1]: "The United States is allocated an additional 25 mt in 2025 and 62.5 mt in 2026 to account for bycatch related to pelagic longline fisheries."
- D03 (bluefin tuna quota section, source of the new allocation) [c1]: "this allocation is derived from the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean bluefin tuna TAC"
- D03 (same paragraph, earlier treatment) [c1]: "Recommendation 25-05 removed a provision from a prior recommendation that provided for subtracting the longline bycatch allocation from the TAC before calculating the individual country quotas."
- D03 (set-aside section, change of source) [c1]: "Recommendation 25-05 now specifies that the set-aside comes from the eastern Atlantic bluefin tuna TAC as opposed to the western Atlantic TAC."
sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h10 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i07, found by the independent question-author run
  (2026-10-10) and re-verified by the caller against D03 L124-127, L172-176 and D06 Table 5, L185, L209, L212.
  Medium target, Hard welcome (user 2026-10-10). Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: D06 Table 5 prints, for 2025 and 2026, the baseline quota (1,316.14; 1,509.98) and the
  total quota with the pelagic longline bycatch allocation (1,341.14; 1,572.48), then the adjusted quotas
  (1,199.94; 1,647.28). D03 says where each bycatch allocation comes from: the new 62.5 mt from the eastern
  Atlantic and Mediterranean TAC, the earlier one from the western Atlantic TAC (subtracted from that TAC
  before country quotas were calculated). So the western-TAC tonnage is 1,316.14 + 25 = 1,341.14 mt for 2025
  and 1,509.98 mt for 2026: 168.84 mt more.
- Universe: not applicable (one number). Candidate figures per year, all in Table 5: baseline, total, adjusted.
- Necessity: D06 -> the 2025 figures. "1,316.14" and "1,341.14" appear only in D06 (Grep, seven texts). D03
  prints the superseded 2025 subquotas (710.7, 59.2, 209.3, 1.3) and the category percentages, which rebuild
  the old baseline only to a range of about 1,316.04-1,316.20 (168.78-168.94), not to two decimals. D03 -> the
  origin of the earlier allocation. "as opposed to the western Atlantic TAC" and "subtracting the longline
  bycatch allocation from the TAC" appear only in D03; D06 says only that the new allocation is "derived from
  the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean bluefin tuna TAC" (L212) and calls the earlier one "the 25-mt set-aside
  for the Northeast Distant gear restricted area (NED)". Without D03 nothing in the bundle decides between
  168.84 and 193.84. Stated risks: the 2025 U.S. baseline quota (1,316.14 mt) appeared in earlier Federal
  Register notices and may be recalled; a solver without D03 faces a two-way choice. Optional closed-book
  diagnostic (2026-10-10, runs/q04-r0-diagnostics/closed-book.md, partial contamination reported): answer
  174.24, not the gold, but the return recalls 1,316.14 mt, the 25 mt allowance, that it came out of the
  western TAC ("2,726 t ... less 40 t of bycatch set-asides") and the 2026 TAC 3,081.6 t. So with either
  ticked document left out, the other plus recall can reach 168.84: the form's "Needs two or more documents"
  check may report Doc 3 or Doc 6 as not needed. Run the form's full checks before spending a difficulty run.
- Selected-lever checks: Match, then exclude. Exclusion skipped (both bycatch allocations counted):
  1,572.48 - 1,341.14 = 231.34. Exclusion applied to both years: 1,509.98 - 1,316.14 = 193.84. Correct, one
  year each: 168.84. All three differ.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Part vs total: 193.84, the baseline pair that D06's Comment 1 prints side by
  side. (2) Wrong jurisdiction or scope: 231.34, the Total Quota row, which counts tonnage from the eastern
  TAC. Considered and not declared, because the lead clause rules them out: the Adjusted Quota row (1,647.28
  - 1,199.94 = 447.34) and mixed forms (310.04, 384.84, 409.84). Align the declared modes with the run's
  observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: script (Decimal), 2026-10-10: 1316.14 + 25 = 1341.14 (equals the printed 2025
  Total Quota); 1509.98 - 1341.14 = 168.84. Cross-check of the 2026 base: 3,081.6 x 0.49 = 1,509.984 (D03
  L124). Units mt whole weight; positive; exact at two decimals.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 168.84, 193.84 or 231.34. "western Atlantic TAC" lands on
  D03 L176, an input passage. The capture's overview lists 1,509.98 and 62.5 for both documents and neither
  2025 figure. Shortest complete route found: the two calculations after the two source decisions.
- Precision/readings: "allocated ... before any underharvest or overharvest adjustment" excludes the adjusted
  quotas; "of the western Atlantic bluefin tuna total allowable catch" is the condition that keeps 2025's 25
  mt and drops 2026's 62.5 mt, both per D03. A reading that drops the 25 mt as well (193.84) contradicts
  D03's statement that the earlier allocation was subtracted from that TAC; a reading that keeps the 62.5 mt
  (231.34) contradicts D03 L126 and D06 L212. The 2025 TAC itself is not printed and is not needed.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps.
- Document roles: both Answer component. D03 supplies no operand; it supplies the two facts that fix the
  operands (the earlier 25 mt was western TAC tonnage, the new 62.5 mt is not), the same way rule-giving
  documents were ticked on aq-02564 q02. If a reviewer asks for the other role, "Exclusion / condition
  source" with the note "only document saying the earlier 25 mt bycatch allocation came out of the western
  Atlantic TAC while the new 62.5 mt does not" is the alternative.
- Style/set review: one ask, 33 words. A different stock, mechanism and answer path from q01-q03 (bluefin,
  no weight conversion); shares only the two documents.
- Warnings answered: form-numbers WARNs expected, since every bluefin figure sits past character 20,000 in
  both documents (D06: 1,509.98 at 20,691, 62.5 at 21,003, 1,316.14 at 33,492; D03: 1,509.98 at 24,729). The
  deepest position the form is known to have read is 19,581, and it flagged figures near 80,000; between the
  two its behaviour is unobserved. If it shows "Doc 6 doesn't mention 1,316.14" or the like, that is the
  expected false alarm: each figure is quoted as evidence from that document.

sections.question: Before any underharvest or overharvest adjustment, how many more metric tons of the western Atlantic bluefin tuna total allowable catch was the United States allocated for 2026 than for 2025, to two decimals?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 6, Table 5 and Comment 1): the U.S. bluefin tuna baseline quota is 1,316.14 mt for 2025 and 1,509.98 mt for 2026, before any carryover.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 6, note to Table 5): on top of the baseline quota the United States is allocated an additional 25 mt in 2025 and 62.5 mt in 2026 for pelagic longline bycatch.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, bluefin tuna quota section): the new bycatch allocation is derived from the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean bluefin tuna TAC, so for 2026 the U.S. tonnage out of the western Atlantic TAC is the baseline quota alone.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 3, bluefin tuna quota section and set-aside section): the set-aside now comes from the eastern TAC "as opposed to the western Atlantic TAC", and the earlier recommendation subtracted the longline bycatch allocation from the TAC before the country quotas were calculated. The earlier bycatch allocation was therefore western Atlantic TAC tonnage and counts for 2025.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 6 and Doc 3): U.S. western Atlantic tonnage for 2025: 1,316.14 + 25 = 1,341.14 mt, the 2025 Total Quota that Table 5 prints.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 6 and Doc 3): increase from 2025 to 2026: 1,509.98 - 1,341.14 = 168.84 mt.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Part vs total: Doc 6 Table 5's Baseline row alone gives 193.84, dropping 2025's 25 mt. Wrong scope: its Total row gives 231.34, counting 2026's 62.5 mt that Doc 3 says comes from the eastern TAC, unlike the earlier set-aside. Gold: 1,509.98 - 1,341.14 = 168.84.
